quests.question: A watch that costs a lot of money is…
quests.explanation: Expensive means costing a lot, and it is the opposite of cheap, which means low in price.

quests.question: The opposite of "tight" for a shirt?
quests.explanation: Tight clothes fit closely to the body, while loose clothes hang freely and feel roomy and comfortable.

quests.question: Closest in meaning to "talk"?
quests.explanation: Talk and speak both mean to say words aloud, like talking to a friend on the phone.

quests.question: The opposite of "hot"?
quests.explanation: Hot means very high in temperature, and cold means very low, like cold water on a hot day.

quests.question: The detective found strong ___ that the man lied.
quests.explanation: Evidence is the facts or signs that show something is true. A rumour is only unproven talk.

quests.question: Closest in meaning to "honest"?
quests.explanation: Honest and truthful both describe someone who tells the truth, even when it is not easy to say.

quests.question: The ___ of the building took two years.
quests.explanation: After "The" and before "of" we need a noun. Construction is the noun, and constructive means helpful.

quests.question: The burglar ___ across the dark room so nobody would hear.
quests.explanation: To creep is to move slowly and quietly so nobody hears you, which is exactly what a burglar tries to do.

quests.question: Three of these describe something not big. Odd one out?
quests.explanation: Tiny, slight and minor all mean small, while immense means extremely large, so it is the odd one out.

quests.question: The person you work alongside is your…
quests.explanation: A colleague is someone you work alongside in the same organisation. A rival competes against you.

quests.question: A long formal piece of academic writing for a degree:
quests.explanation: A dissertation is a long, formal piece of academic writing for a degree. A memo is a short workplace note.

quests.question: The opposite of "frugal"?
quests.explanation: Frugal means spending as little as possible, while lavish means spending freely or extravagantly.

quests.question: Someone who refuses to consider others' ideas is…
quests.explanation: A closed-minded person will not listen to new views. Receptive, curious and attentive people stay open to them.

quests.question: Which is the mildest way of trying to stop something?
quests.explanation: To discourage is to try to persuade someone not to do something. Forbid, ban and prohibit stop it by rule.

quests.question: Closest in meaning to "polite"?
quests.explanation: Courteous means polite and considerate, like a courteous waiter who always listens and says thank you.

quests.question: Someone who applies for a job is an…
quests.explanation: An applicant is someone applying for a job. An employee already has one, and an employer gives it out.

quests.question: Speaking up clearly without attacking others is…
quests.explanation: Assertive is a positive word for speaking up clearly and respectfully. Bossy and aggressive are negative.

quests.question: The company is known for its ___ in the tech industry.
quests.explanation: After "its" we need a noun for the quality. Innovation names the act of creating new ideas and products.

quests.question: Money paid regularly after you stop working is a…
quests.explanation: A pension is a regular payment to retired workers. A premium is the regular cost of an insurance plan.

quests.question: To strongly and publicly support a cause is to…
quests.explanation: To champion a cause is to defend and promote it strongly and publicly. Oppose and abandon are the reverse.

quests.question: To cause something to start is to…
quests.explanation: To initiate is to begin or set something in motion, like starting a new project. Halt and cancel stop it.

quests.question: A person who takes part in an activity is a…
quests.explanation: A participant takes part in an activity, while a spectator only watches it from the side.

quests.question: Closest in meaning to "mundane"?
quests.explanation: Mundane describes dull, everyday tasks like washing dishes, so everyday is the closest word in meaning.

quests.question: The opposite of "immaculate"?
quests.explanation: Immaculate means perfectly clean, while grubby means dirty. Spotless and pristine are close to immaculate.

quests.question: Closest in meaning to "copious"?
quests.explanation: Copious means more than enough, like copious notes, and abundant carries the same idea.

quests.question: To give formal approval to an agreement is to…
quests.explanation: To ratify is to give formal approval that makes an agreement official, like countries ratifying a treaty.

quests.question: A quick, secretive look is…
quests.explanation: Furtive means done in a secret, sneaky way, like a quick glance you hope nobody else notices at all.

quests.question: He gave a ___ apology, only because his boss was watching.
quests.explanation: Grudging means done unwillingly, like an apology made only because the boss was watching the whole time.

quests.question: Which word shows the MOST intense worry?
quests.explanation: To agonise is to suffer deep anxiety while thinking a problem over. Fret is milder, and wonder is calm.

quests.question: To speak of something as having little value is to…
quests.explanation: To disparage is to speak of something as having little value, which belittles it unfairly in public.
